absent: Locking, interrupt safety and concurrency rules for checksum, user access window, clock and vclock operations.
Data layouts of network address, clocksource, clock event device and user pointer types.
Exception table registration, fixup addresses and precise fault versus success side effects on partial copies.
Build selection between alternate 32 bit checksum implementations and between 32 bit and 64 bit headers.

Lifecycle and ordering requirements for virtual clock usage bits.

findings.text: Combined copy plus checksum service moves a caller length from source to destination while accumulating an intermediate Internet checksum value for later folding, with distinct 32 bit and 64 bit implementations sharing that contract.
Incremental checksum service folds a buffer of caller length into a caller supplied seed and returns the updated intermediate sum, accepting arbitrary alignment and length.
User buffer helpers expose checksum plus copy toward and from user memory, are callable in sleepable context, validate the user range first, and report failure with a zero checksum result.
User access window helpers open and close a bounded region where user memory may be touched, with the open operation reporting success or failure to the caller.
Folding and word addition helpers expose reduction of an intermediate sum to final complement form and addition with end around carry for 32 bit checksum words.
Network header helpers expose fast IP header checksum, full buffer IP checksum, TCP UDP pseudo header accumulation with and without final fold, and IPv6 pseudo header final checksum.
Unaligned word load helper exposes a single machine word fetch that yields zero padded data when the access faults near the end of a mapping.

Inlined clock helpers expose a direct ordered timestamp read for a clocksource and a direct deadline write for a coupled clock event device, plus query and mark operations over a global virtual clock usage bitmap.

Atomic exchange style macro exposes a size dispatched operation that applies a caller chosen mnemonic with a caller chosen lock prefix to a pointed to object and returns the prior value, rejecting unsupported sizes.

User access is only enabled after range validation succeeds; on validation failure the helper reports failure and does not enable the access window, and successful windows are always explicitly closed after the copy.
Enabling the user access window also issues a speculation barrier, so transient execution cannot bypass the access enable sequence.

Checksum accumulation preserves end around carry across bulk and tail processing and normalizes carry between stages, with final reduction combining high and low halves and complementing where a final checksum is required.

Misaligned starts and odd lengths are normalized by consuming a small leading prefix and by rotating the accumulated value by one byte when the buffer start or residual length is odd, so the result is independent of alignment.

The 64 bit incremental path uses parallel wide accumulation for large inputs, a direct path for a common medium header size, power of two remainder handling, and masked handling of a short non word tail before final folding.
Virtual clock usage is represented as one bit per clock index in a shared global, tested by shifting by the queried index and set by read modify write of the same global.

Potentially faulting source, destination and prefetch accesses in the copy and checksum paths are associated with exception fixups that abandon the accumulation and return a zero checksum, and the tail word load uses a zero pad fixup instead of faulting.

Copy checksum processing behaves as alignment normalization followed by bulk accumulation followed by progressively narrower remainder handling with carry normalization and odd byte adjustment before return or fault exit.
Assembly checksum entries preserve caller saved registers on entry, read buffer and length and seed through fixed stack slots, and restore the saved state before returning the checksum result.
Object size dispatch uses numeric codes one and two and four for byte and word and long, with eight selecting quad on one build and a negative sentinel disabling quad on the other build.
Architecture advertises native IPv6 checksum and checksum addition capability through feature macros and protects checksum and clock and command line headers with include guard macros.
